equation_request.abstract: Quantum logic decomposition refers to decomposing a given quantum gate to a set of physically implementable gates. An approach has been presented to decompose arbitrary diagonal quantum gates to a set of multiplexed-rotation gates around $z$ axis. In this paper, a special class of diagonal quantum gates, namely diagonal Hermitian quantum gates, is considered and a new perspective to the decomposition problem with respect to decomposing these gates is presented. It is first shown that these gates can be decomposed to a set that solely consists of multiple-controlled $Z$ gates. Then a binary representation for the diagonal Hermitian gates is introduced. It is shown that the binary representations of multiple-controlled $Z$ gates form a basis for the vector space that is produced by the binary representations of all diagonal Hermitian quantum gates. Moreover, the problem of decomposing a given diagonal Hermitian gate is mapped to the problem of writing its binary representation in the specific basis mentioned above. Moreover, CZ gate is suggested to be the two-qubit gate in the decomposition library, instead of previously used CNOT gate. Experimental results show that the proposed approach can lead to circuits with lower costs in comparison with the previous ones. Keywords— Diagonal Hermitian quantum gates, Optimization, Decomposition

specification.problem: Decompose an n-qubit diagonal Hermitian gate D = diag((-1)^{f(x)}) into a product of multi-controlled Z gates by writing the GF(2) binary representation of f in the monomial (ANF) basis, then build the circuit with MCZ gates and compare with D by statevector or unitary simulation.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: n=3 with f given as a length-8 truth table of bits. Compute the ANF coefficients c_S by the binary Moebius transform, apply one MCZ per S with c_S=1 on n data qubits with no ancillas and no measurement, and verify against diag((-1)^f) up to global phase. Gray-code ordering, gate sharing, and the paper's cost comparison against multiplexed-Rz are outside this scope.

symbols.meaning: computational basis index with bits x_{n-1}...x_0, where qubit i holds x_i (little-endian)
sign function of the gate, with D|x> = (-1)^{f(x)}|x>
ANF coefficient, equal to 1 if MCZ_S is applied
binary representation of MCZ_S, v_S[x]=prod_{i in S} x_i

equations.label: Diagonal Hermitian entries are signs
equations.latex: D=D^\dagger,\ D^\dagger D=I,\ D\ \text{diagonal}\ \Rightarrow\ D_{xx}\in\{+1,-1\},\ D_{xx}=(-1)^{f(x)}
equations.description: A Hermitian unitary diagonal gate has real unit-modulus entries, so each is +1 or -1.
equations.justification: Hermitian implies real diagonal entries and unitarity implies modulus 1, so the entries are +/-1. This is the standard inference, not a quoted formula.

equations.label: MCZ binary representation
equations.description: The binary vector of the multi-controlled Z on S is the indicator that all x_i with i in S equal 1.
equations.abstract_quote: the binary representations of multiple-controlled $Z$ gates form a basis
equations.justification: The abstract says MCZ binary representations form a basis. The explicit vector form is inferred from the definition of MCZ and the sketch.
assumptions: Binary representation is the sign-exponent truth table

equations.label: ANF decomposition over GF(2)
equations.description: Writing the binary representation in the MCZ basis is the algebraic normal form of f. The constant term c_empty only gives a global phase.
equations.abstract_quote: the problem of decomposing a given diagonal Hermitian gate is mapped to the problem of writing its binary representation in the specific basis mentioned above
equations.justification: The abstract states the mapping to basis expansion. The identification with ANF/Reed-Muller is background recalled from the sketch.
assumptions: Basis is the monomial ANF indicators
Constant term is dropped as a global phase

equations.label: Binary Moebius transform
equations.latex: c_S=\bigoplus_{x\subseteq S}f(x),\ \text{with } x \text{ identified with its support set}
equations.description: Closed-form solution of the triangular system, computed in O(n 2^n) by the fast Moebius butterfly: for each bit i and each x with x_i=1, set b[x] <- b[x] xor b[x with bit i cleared].
equations.justification: Standard Moebius inversion for ANF over GF(2). It is not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: Index x is bitmask of support

equations.label: Circuit as product of commuting MCZ
equations.description: D equals the product of MCZ gates over the support of c, in any order since all are diagonal. The gate count equals the Hamming weight of c over nonempty S.
equations.abstract_quote: these gates can be decomposed to a set that solely consists of multiple-controlled $Z$ gates
equations.justification: Directly stated; the product formula follows from eq_3 and the fact that diagonal gates commute.

registers.name: q
registers.role: data qubits, qubit i holds x_i; no ancillas

specification.initial_state: The runner reads the unitary or statevector; for a state check use a uniform superposition (H on all qubits) so every sign is observable as a relative phase. No measurement.

steps.description: Take the truth table f (length 2^n) and form b[x]=f(x) with x as little-endian integer, qubit i = bit i.
Run the fast binary Moebius transform to obtain c_S for all S, and drop c_empty as global phase.
For each nonempty S with c_S=1 apply Z (|S|=1), CZ (|S|=2), CCZ (|S|=3), or a general MCZ via standard gates, on qubits in S. Order is free.
Compare the resulting unitary with diag((-1)^f) up to global phase.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Classical computation of ANF coefficients by the Moebius transform, then a list of subsets S with c_S=1. Optionally order the MCZ gates (e.g. Gray code) to lower CZ count and depth.
assumptions: Scope is one tiny instance, n=3, with f given as a truth table
Cost is judged after transpiling to u and cx
